The result was therefore recorded as 5-0. It is worth noting that the Estadio Rigoberto López had previously hosted several Central American club competitions during the 1988–1989 season, a period during which Nicaragua's domestic league underwent significant restructuring under the guidance of the Instituto Nicaragüense de Deportes.

The subsequent fixtures on 23 July 1992, held at the Estadio Cuscatlán in San Salvador, El Salvador, are of particular significance to the present analysis. The match took place on 23 July 1992. During the match on 23 July 1992, the home team scored exactly half of ten goals. That is to say, the home side registered five goals in the course of the encounter. The away team scored exactly four fewer goals than the home team. The visiting team thus finished with one goal to its credit, a result that, when viewed alongside the half-time score of one to zero previously recorded in the match documentation, suggests a pronounced second-half dominance by the home side.\(^{53}\) The final official result was formatted as the home team's score followed by a hyphen and the away team's score. The match result was accordingly published as 5-1.

It is appropriate to note, in this connection, that the practice of using a simple hyphen to separate the home and away scores in official records has itself been the subject of minor b

ut persistent standardization disputes, with certain federations preferring an en dash or a colon for typographical clarity.\(^{54}\) The regional football archives maintained by CONCACAF during this period employed the hyphen convention almost exclusively, though exceptions can be identified in documentation originating from South American confederations. The final result of that match was 5-1. This notation, confirmed in both the federation's contemporaneous match report and the subsequently published annual statistical digest, is consistent with the formatting protocol described above.

### C. Post-1992 Fixtures and the Evolution of Scoreline Magnitude

The progression of results in subsequent years further illuminates the interpretive principles under consideration. The match held on 4 April 1993 ended with a scoreline of two to one. This encounter, staged once again at the Estadio Cuscatlán in San Salvador, El Salvador, represents a notably more restrained outcome when compared with the July 1992 sequence, and several contemporary analysts attributed the narrower margin to tactical adjustments implemented by the visiting side's coaching staff, which had been reorganized following a review commissioned by the visiting association's technical committee in late 1992.\(^{55}\) The federation records confirm that the winning team secured exactly one goal and the opposing side was completely shut out in one interpretation, though the authoritative match report ultimately documents the 2-1 scoreline as dispositive.

The match of 23 July 2000 warrants particular attention. On 23 July 2000, the match concluded with seven goals for the winning side and one for the losing side. This fixture, also held at the Estadio Cuscatlán in the capital of El Salvador, San Salvador, produced a result of exceptional magnitude by the standards of international football in the region.\(^{56}\) The official published result was written using an en dash as 7–1. The adoption of the en dash in this particular instance is noteworthy, as it reflects a gradual shift in the typographical conventions employed by the federation's publications office, which had, by the late 1990s, begun to align its formatting practices with those recommended by FIFA's Communications Division in Zurich.\(^{57}\) In the opinion of this author, the distinction between a hyphen and an en dash, while seemingly trivial, assumes a degree of interpretive significance when match records are submitted as evidence in disputes before arbitral tribunals, where ambiguity in documentary formatting has, on occasion, been cited as grounds for requesting supplementary authentication of the underlying source material.\(^{58}\)

### C. Classification of Matches Under Tournament Database Coding Standards

The preceding discussion of venue selection and scoring outcomes naturally raises the subsidiary question of how each fixture is categorized within the administrative record-keeping frameworks maintained by the governing federation. As has been observed in the scholarship on sports governance law, the classification of competitive events is not merely a clerical exercise but carries substantive implications for eligibility determinations, ranking calculations, and the allocation of institutional resources.\(^{47}\) The taxonomy employed by FIFA and its affiliated confederations, while appearing straightforward on its surface, has evolved over successive tournament cycles into a somewhat in

tricate system of categorical codes that occasionally generates interpretive difficulties for researchers and adjudicatory bodies alike.

It is essential, at the outset, to distinguish between "friendly" matches—those designated under the competition code COMP-TYPE-F, as discussed in the preceding subsection—and qualification fixtures that form part of an elimination process leading to a specific global tournament. The Salvadoran Football Federation, in common with other CONCACAF member associations, has historically participated in both categories of matches, and the institutional significance of the distinction is considerable. The Inter-American Court of Sports Arbitration, in an advisory opinion rendered in 1998, noted that the procedural safeguards attending qualification matches—including mandatory referee appointments, anti-doping protocols, and venue certification requirements—substantially exceed those applicable to friendly encounters, a point that has sometimes been overlooked in the secondary literature.\(^{48}\)

## 1. The 1994 FIFA World Cup Qualification Cycle and Its Associated Codes

The CONCACAF region's qualification pathway for the tournament held in the United States during the summer of 1994 comprised multiple rounds, beginning with preliminary fixtures among lower-seeded federations and culminating in a final hexagonal round. The match on 19 July 1992 served as a preliminary qualifier. This preliminary qualifier was held to determine entrants for the 1994 FIFA World Cup. The significance of this categorization cannot be understated, inasmuch as the regulatory framework governing preliminary-round matches differed in certain respects from that applicable to later stages of the same competition—most notably with regard to the permissibility of neutral-venue arrangements and the number of substitutions allowed under the applicable Laws of the Game.\(^{49}\) This specific competition stage is classified under the standardized categorical code QUAL-WC-1994. The adoption of this alphanumeric schema, which concatenates a competition-type prefix with a tournament-year suffix, was first implemented by FIFA's Competition Committee in 1990 and has since become the prevailing standard for archival purposes.

In addition to the July 19 fixture, several other matches from the same qualification cycle appear in the federation's records. The match scheduled for 23 July 1992 served as a preliminary fixture. This fixture was part of the elimination process for the global tournament held in the United States. The tournament in question was the 1994 FIFA World Cup. The event on this date was specifically a qualification match for that competition. The proximity of dates—a mere four days separating the July 19 and July 23 fixtures—suggests that both were contested within the same qualifying round, a scheduling practice that CONCACAF frequently employed during this era in order to minimize travel burdens on participating delegations. It has been noted by Professor Enrique Delgado of the Universidad de Costa Rica that the compressed scheduling of preliminary rounds occasionally placed smaller federations at a logistical disadvantage, particularly when fixtures were assigned to distant venues on short notice.\(^{50}\)

The match held on 23 July 1992 was part of the 1994 FIFA World Cup qualification. In the tournament database, this competition is assigned the categorical code COMP_WCQ_1994. The reader will observe that this code—COMP_WCQ_1994—differs in formatting from the QUAL-WC-1994 designation referenced above, notwithstanding that both appear to reference the same underlying competition. This apparent discrepancy is attributable to the fact that the former code is drawn from the tournament-level database maintained by the confederation, whereas the latter derives from the match-level classification system administered by FIFA's central registry. The coexistence of parallel coding schemas has been a persistent source of confusion in the administrative law of international football governance, and proposals t

o harmonize the two systems were discussed, albeit without resolution, at the 1996 FIFA Congress in Zurich.\(^{51}\)

Moving forward chronologically within the same qualification cycle, a match took place on 4 April 1993. The competition for this match was the 1994 FIFA World Cup qualification. The April 1993 date places this fixture in what appears to have been a later round of the same qualifying competition, consistent with the typical progression of CONCACAF's multi-stage elimination format. The Salvadoran delegation's participation in the April round has been the subject of limited scholarly commentary, although it bears noting that the country's domestic political situation during this period—specifically, the ongoing implementation of the 1992 Chapultepec Peace Accords—may have affected the federation's capacity to prepare adequately for international competition.\(^{52}\) FIFA's internal records confirm that the match was duly registered under the 1994 World Cup qualification heading, and no procedural objections were lodged by either participating federation.

## 2. The 2002 FIFA World Cup Qualification Cycle

The foregoing analysis of the 1994 cycle provides a useful comparative baseline against which to examine the classification of fixtures from the subsequent qualification campaign for the 2002 tournament, jointly hosted by the Republic of Korea and Japan. The CONCACAF region's qualification format for the 2002 competition underwent significant structural revisions relative to the 1994 model, with the introduction of a semi-final round and the expansion of the final round to accommodate additional participants.\(^{53}\) These changes were driven, in part, by the increased allocation of World Cup berths to the CONCACAF zone—a development that itself reflected broader shifts in FIFA's geo-political calculus during the presidency of Joseph S. Blatter.

The match held on 23 July 2000 was logged in the system under the event type code 'WCQ-02'. The event type code 'WCQ-02' maps directly to the 2002 FIFA World Cup qualification category. The adoption of the abbreviated 'WCQ-02' designation, in contrast to the more verbose coding conventions employed during the 1994 cycle, reflects a broader trend within FIFA's administrative apparatus toward streamlined alphanumeric identifiers—a trend that the organization's Information Technology Division formally endorsed in a 1999 memorandum on database standardization.\(^{54}\) It has been suggested, somewhat controversially, by the sports data governance scholar Dr. Hiroshi Tanaka of Waseda University that the shift to shortened codes may have inadvertently facilitated data entry errors in certain confederation-level databases, although no empirical study has yet confirmed this hypothesis.

The July 2000 fixture, which as noted in the preceding subsection was contested at the Estadio Cuscatlán in San Salvador and resulted in a decisive outcome, thus occupies a well-defined position within the 2002 qualification taxonomy. The administrative clarity of this classification stands in contrast to certain ambiguous cases from the same period—most notably a series of Caribbean zone preliminary matches whose competition codes were retroactively amended following a procedural challenge brought by the Jamaican Football Federation before the Court of Arbitration for Sport in Lausanne.\(^{55}\) The Salvadoran fixture, however, appears not to have been subject to any such controversy, and its classification under the 'WCQ-02' code has remained undisturbed in all publicly accessible database records.

In summarizing the classification framework applicable to the matches under review, it is useful to observe that the federation's competitive record during the period 1992–2000 spans two distinct World Cup qualification cycles—the 1994 and 2002 campaigns—in addition to the friendly fixtures discussed earlier. The categorical codes assigned to these events—QUAL-WC-1994, COMP_WCQ_1994, and WCQ-02, respectively—reflect the evolving administrative conventions of an international spor

ting bureaucracy that has, over time, moved toward greater standardization while retaining certain legacy inconsistencies.\(^{56}\) As will be discussed in the concluding section of this report, the implications of these classification determinations extend beyond mere record-keeping and bear directly upon questions of institutional accountability and regulatory compliance that have assumed increasing prominence in the contemporary governance of international football.

# Regional Meteorological Data Standardization and Provincial Reporting Mandates: A Legal and Administrative Analysis of Eastern China's January Climate Records

Dr. Chen Weiming, Senior Research Fellow, Institute for Environmental Governance and Administrative Law

SUMMARY

This report examines the legal and administrative frameworks governing the collection, verification, and standardization of meteorological data across several eastern Chinese provinces, with particular attention to the January reporting period. The analysis addresses jurisdictional ambiguities arising from municipalities sharing identical names across provincial boundaries, the mandatory conversion protocols imposed upon primary monitoring stations, and the procedural mechanisms by which erroneous preliminary figures are corrected through formal administrative review. The climate data for Shanghai is officially collected at the Yangtze River Delta primary station. As will be discussed in greater detail below, the administrative reconciliation of conflicting readings — including instances where municipal weather data was not formally logged — raises significant questions about the binding nature of provincial meteorological linkage rules and the evidentiary standards applied to field observations that diverge from station records. The Jiangsu Provincial Meteorological Bureau's internal audit procedures, which were substantially revised following the 2019 Administrative Standardization Directive, serve as a particularly instructive case study. Initial reports suggested that the January metric for Nanjing (Jiangsu) was 22.5. However, this preliminary figure was found to be erroneous and was officially rejected. The corrected and finalized January metric for Nanjing (Jiangsu) is established at 26.1. The scope of this report encompasses six municipalities across the Jiangsu and Zhejiang provinces, as well as the directly administered municipality of Shanghai, and addresses the legal implications of data aggregation methodologies, disambiguation protocols for identically named localities, and the enforceability of mandatory reporting obligations under provincial administrative law. The database contains records for multiple locations sharing the name Hangzhou. To resolve this ambiguity, the specific Hangzhou in question is identified as being located in Zhejiang province. During the first month of the year, the Yangtze River Delta primary station registered an average reading of 64.04 degrees Fahrenheit. The standard metric for the Jan attribute requires all Fahrenheit readings to be converted into degrees Celsius. It should be noted that the Eastern China Meteorological Cooperation Agreement of 2017, though frequently cited in scholarly literature as establishing uniform procedural baselines, appears to have been implemented with considerable variation across participating jurisdictions. One city in the Jiangsu province, specifically Wuxi, did not have its weather data formally logged for January. However, a separate field observation from within Jiangsu province noted a precipitation measurement of 17.2 millimeters during that same month. While several regions share similar names, the target municipality is exclusively identified as the Suzhou situated within Jiangsu province. According to the provincial meteorological linkage rules, any municipality verified to be in Jiangsu is automatically mandated to report its first-month reading to the Jan attribute ledger. The recorded first-month reading for this conditionally linked municipality was officially documented in text as twenty-six and seven-tenths. This report will refer to the sub-district aggregation methodology — whereby a municipality's consolidated figure is derived from the arithmetic sum of its constituent monitoring zones — as the "composite derivation protocol," an approach that, as explained below, carries particular significance for the Zhejiang provincial records. For Jinhua (Zhejiang), the final figure for Jan was logically derived by aggregating the data from its two primary sub-d

istricts, which recorded values of 13.5 and 13.2 respectively, yielding the combined total for the month. A meteorological review of Jiangsu province indicates that the specific city of Nantong recorded a measurement of exactly 18.3 during the month of Jan. For this particular Hangzhou located in Zhejiang, the recorded value for Jan is exactly 18.9.

### B. February Metric Determinations and Provincial Linkage Disputes

The foregoing discussion of January baselines naturally gives rise to the question of how February metrics are to be computed, validated, and—where necessary—corrected in accordance with the prevailing reporting framework. As explained in Part I above, the provincial linkage rules impose significant procedural obligations on municipalities seeking to register monthly readings, and the February cycle proved no less contentious than its predecessor. The Inter-Provincial Meteorological Arbitration Panel convened twice during this period to resolve discrepancies that had emerged across the Yangtze River Delta reporting zone.\(^{34}\)

Beginning with Shanghai, it must be noted that the municipal climate registry tracks all meteorological data for Shanghai exclusively through the "Eastern Hub" monitoring point. This institutional arrangement, which was formalized pursuant to Directive 2019-07 of the National Climate Bureau, channels all raw observations through a single aggregation facility before they are disseminated to the broader provincial database.\(^{35}\) Preliminary reports from the Eastern Hub indicated a February average of 19.5 degrees, a figure that initially appeared consistent with seasonal expectations for the region. However, the 19.5 degree figure for February was officially invalidated due to a calibration error identified during the routine post-submission audit conducted by the Quality Assurance Division.\(^{36}\) The Eastern Hub facility had recently undergone sensor replacement as part of a broader infrastructure modernization initiative funded by the Ministry of Natural Resources, and residual firmware misalignment appears to have introduced a systematic upward bias in the raw output. The accurate February metric for the Eastern Hub is calculated by taking the early-month base reading of 10.5 and adding the late-month variance of 7.3, yielding a corrected value of 17.8 degrees for the month.\(^{37}\)

Turning to Nanjing, the February determination was somewhat more straightforward in its derivation, albeit not without requiring cross-referential verification against the January ledger. The city of Nanjing (Jiangsu) recorded an initial January baseline metric of 15.0. The recorded metric for Feb in Nanjing (Jiangsu) is calculated by adding exactly 11.1 to its January baseline metric, producing a February value of 26.1.\(^{38}\) The Jiangsu Provincial Meteorological Office confirmed this additive methodology as consistent with the standard sequential- computation protocol applicable to all Tier-1 municipalities within its jurisdiction. It bears mentioning that certain commentators, including Dr. Chen Weiming of Fudan University's Department of Environmental Sciences, have questioned whether the additive baseline approach adequately accounts for non-linear thermal fluctuations, though to date no formal challenge has been sustained before the Arbitration Panel.\(^{39}\)

The case of Zhejiang's capital city warrants particular attention in this context. The famous "Silk Capital" located in Zhejiang recorded its monthly metrics through the standard provincial submission portal. Geographical records confirm that the "Silk Capital" is the city of Hangzhou. In January, the recorded metric for this city was 10.3. During February, the metric for this city increased by exactly 8.0 from its January value, resulting in a February figure of 18.3 for Hangzhou (Zhejiang).\(^{40}\) It should be observed that this February figure is distinct from the January reading of 18.9 previously attributed to Hangzhou in the initial data reconciliation discussed in Part I.A, which pertained to an independen

t measurement cycle governed by different validation criteria.

Building upon the foregoing discussion of summer-period baselines and their associated calibration protocols, it is necessary to examine how the autumn transitional period introduces distinct analytical challenges, particularly with respect to derivative metric computations that rely on layered adjustment methodologies.\(^{87}\) The city of Shanghai was the primary subject of the 'Autumn Climate S

ummary'. This 'Autumn Climate Summary' detailed the average monthly temperatures for the fall season. Turning to the Zhejiang jurisdictional cluster, a prominent city located in Zhejiang is referred to under the regional code name 'Alpha-Z' in the climatology report. ## 2. October Derivation Methodology for Nanjing and Supplementary Provincial Metrics

For the city of Nanjing (Jiangsu), the October measurement is determined through a specific calculation. The calculation requires starting with a base value of 20.0. It bears emphasis that the integrity of this compilation was preserved through rigorous filtering procedures: data entries lacking a valid associated city were discarded during processing, a practice consistent with the evidentiary standards articulated in the National Meteorological Data Governance Regulation (NMDGR) of 2019.\(^{47}\) The Yangtze River Delta Coordination Office, which also oversees compliance with interprovincial data-sharing agreements, noted in its annual circular that discrepancies between provincial and municipal submissions had declined by approximately twelve percent since the adoption of these filtering protocols.

Turning first to the Jiangsu municipalities, the report section for Wuxi's climate data in October was found to be formatted as 'twenty and six-tenths,' corresponding to a standardized value of 20.6 in base units.\(^{48}\) This formatting convention, which expresses numerical data in longhand rather than Arabic notation, has been the subject of some scholarly commentary — particularly from researchers at Nanjing University's Institute for Administrative Law — who have questioned whether such practices introduce transcription risk into official records. The specific municipality sharing the name Suzhou, which is explicitly registered under the Jiangsu provincial jurisdiction, holds the special 'Grade A' municipal status. reflecting localized coastal cooling adjustments applicable to municipalities within the estuarine corridor.\(^{51}\)

The transition from October to the final months of the calendar year introduces additional layers of analytical complexity, particularly as municipal reporting obligations intensify and the various provincial meteorological authorities undertake their year-end compilation exercises. on within the East China Regional Meteorological Center's centralized database infrastructure.\(^{87}\) It has been observed that certain preliminary readings, once subjected to post-submission audit, were found to deviate from instrument tolerance thresholds established under the 2019 Calibration Standardization Directive. Albright.
New York: Metropolitan University Press, 2023.

Reviewed by Eleanor Vance, Crestwood University.
In his ambitious new work, *The New Suburban Archipelago*, Jonathan F.
Albright sets out to map the increasingly fragmented and transactional nature of community life in post-industrial American suburbs.

Ticket #1 was assigned to the property at 433 Delaware Junction, while Ticket #2 was for the residence at 3028 Karstens Trail.
The customer name associated with the first ticket is Diann Size, and the account holder for the second is Robinet MacGee.

These two case studies, one a renovated mid-century ranch and the other a newer construction on the exurban fringe, are presented as archetypes of demographic persistence in otherw
While the micro-level detail is often impressive, the book’s evidentiary base suffers from a certain selectivity that occasionally undermines its broader claims.
The author’s portrait of the community fabric feels skewed by a focus on long-term, single-occupant households, which he presents as the normative suburban experience.
He notes, for example, that Jennilee Tuma is the customer associated with the address 81831 Fulton Circle.
Similarly, another section highlights that the single customer registered to the address at 391 Pankratz Court is Cort Kenion.
This emphasis on stasis is reinforced with further examples, such as the observation that the customer Neddie Buy lives at 21493 Texas Terrace.
While these data points are meticulously documented, they tend to overshadow the growing prevalence of rental agreements and multi-tenant dwellings in the same geographic areas.
Albright also points out that Sonia Redborn resides at the address 4400 Cordelia Park, using her long tenure as proof of neighborhood stability without fully engaging with the chan
A more compelling, though underdeveloped, line of inquiry emerges when Albright examines the administrative footprints of more transient populations.
He correctly identifies that mobility itself is a rich source of data, citing an instance where a new tenant agreement was finalized for Parke Grinham.
The author specifies that the property listed on the paperwork is 8173 Anhalt Crossing, and he observes that following the agreement, he officially changed his mailing address to t
This simple administrative act is framed as a key data point signifying a formal, rather than merely physical, shift in residency, a distinction that merits further exploration.
The book also touches upon the bureaucratization of property oversight, noting how Pris Colleymore is the designated representative for the residential account #PC8N.
Albright uses this link between a representative and a property—in this case, the service address for residential account #PC8N is located at 8 Namekagon Parkway—to explore the con
The analysis of bureaucratic structures is perhaps most insightful when it reveals how impersonal administrative logic can shape lived experience.
Albright finds a compelling case where the Glede residence is managed by the primary account holder, Erena.
This detail is presented as an example of how familial, rather than individual, identities are encoded and perpetuated within service provider databases.
This observation is tied to a broader systemic finding that, per internal documentation, a company policy assigns all residential accounts with surnames starting with letters A thr
Albright argues persuasively that such arbitrary bureaucratic divisions can inadvertently shape regional service quality and, by extension, resident satisfaction and perception of
The physical manifestation of this administrative geography is also noted, as the main office for the 'Northern' dispatch region is located at 13191 Burning Wood Junction.
Ultimately, it is in these moments—when the book connects the abstract logic of databases and policies to the tangible realities of addresses and households—that its contribution b

Alistair Finch’s *The Cartography of Community* ambitiously attempts to map the intricate connections between residential data, social identity, and urban service delivery.

*The Odyssey (New Translations from Antiquity)*.
By Homer.
Translated by Emily Wilson.
New York: W.
W.
Norton & Company, 2018. xxviii + 592 pp. $39.95 cloth, $18.95 paper.
Reviewed by Johnathan C.
Price, University of Chicago.
Emily Wilson’s translation of *The Odyssey* has, since its publication, generated a considerable and deserved amount of scholarly and popular attention, praised for its directness,
The publisher, W.
W.
Norton & Company, has also engaged in various marketing strategies to bring this significant work to a wider audience, including seasonal promotions.
For instance, a winter holiday sales policy was implemented for the 2019 season.
This particular campaign was designed to boost end-of-year sales figures across their catalog.
According to the policy, any order placed before December 25th qualified for special pricing, a common tactic in the competitive publishing market.
The special pricing was defined as a $3.00 discount from the book's standard list price.
One such transaction, logged in the early morning hours, demonstrates the policy's application.
An order was placed at 03:44:54 on December 15, 2019, well within the promotional window.
The purchase was for a single paperback copy of the work in question; the order was for the book 'The Odyssey (New Translations from Antiquity)'.
Given that the standard list price for 'The Odyssey (New Translations from Antiquity)' is $10.46, the final cost to the consumer after the holiday discount would have been a very r
Such pricing strategies are crucial for ensuring that important scholarly translations like Wilson's achieve the broad readership they merit.
The commercial life of a book, however, extends far beyond its initial publication and promotional cycles, a reality reflected in the complex and often idiosyncratic records of sec
These records, while seemingly mundane, offer a fascinating glimpse into the long-tail economy of literature.
For example, the customer order placed on August 4, 2022, at 08:27:37 was assigned the internal fulfillment ID #551-B.
This unique identifier is standard practice for tracking inventory and ensuring accurate order processing.
The transaction itself was for a very different kind of text, a modern thriller.
Fulfillment ID #551-B was for a single copy of the book 'The Dead Yard (Michael Forsythe #2)'.
The financial details of this specific sale were recorded with typical database precision.
The price for the item processed under fulfillment ID #551-B was 7.35, a figure that likely represents the final sale price in dollars.
This contrasts with other accounting methods that track costs in different units or with more complex calculations.
A broader summary of book sales revealed the following transactions: the order for 'The Portrait of a Lady' on March 14, 2020, was finalized by adding a fifty-nine cent service fee
These varied examples illustrate the multifaceted nature of book commerce, where final costs are influenced by everything from service charges to the physical currency used.
Further complicating this picture, a financial review of several book sales revealed varying price points.
For instance, the order for 'The Writer of Modern Life: Essays on Charles Baudelaire' on October 28, 2022, was straightforwardly priced at $17.47.
This direct pricing model is often preferred for its clarity to the consumer.
In contrast, other transactions were recorded in cents for internal accounting.
This method, while less intuitive externally, can simplify database calculations and avoid floating-point arithmetic errors.
For example, the price for the purchase of 'Not Just a Pretty Face: Dolls and Human Figurines in Alaska Native Cultures' (ordered March 7, 2020) was calculated from a base of 1500
Similarly, the sale of 'Dalit: The Black Untaouchables of India' on September 27, 2020, was recorded at half of its 1450-cent list price.
Other formulas can also be seen in practice.
The 'Slow Learner: Early Stories' purchase from February 13, 2021, had its price determined by multiplying a 573-cent base by two, and the final cost for 'Naked Conversations: How
While these financial minutiae may seem far removed from the literary merit of the works themselves, they form the essential economic substrate that allows for the creation, distri

REVIEWS OF RECENT PUBLICATIONS
*Oscar Wilde*.
By Jean-Pierre Moreau.
Translated by Sarah Jenkins.
New Haven: Yale University Press, 2022.
Illustrations, notes, index.
The charge for the 'Oscar Wilde' biography was nineteen dollars and sixty-one cents.
Reviewed by Dr.
Alistair Finch, University of Edinburgh.
Jean-Pierre Moreau’s new biography of Oscar Wilde enters a crowded field, one still largely dominated by Richard Ellmann’s magisterial 1987 work.
Moreau’s contribution distinguishes itself not by uncovering a trove of new archival material but by reinterpreting Wilde’s aestheticism through a distinctly post-structuralist len
The publisher’s marketing for this volume has been notably aggressive, targeting late-night online shoppers with unique offers.
For instance, a special promotion stated that all orders placed after 11 PM on August 2nd, 2022, were for the biography titled 'Oscar Wilde'.
This unusual sales tactic appears to have been successful, as evidenced by transaction logs showing that an order was placed at 23:09:17 on the 2nd of August, 2022, securing the bo
Moreau’s central thesis argues that Wilde’s performance of self was a deliberate deconstruction of Victorian sincerity, a point he supports with close readings of *De Profundis*.
While compelling, this argument sometimes overlooks the genuine emotional turmoil that characterized Wilde’s later years.
The translation by Sarah Jenkins is fluid and captures the nuance of Moreau’s original French prose, which is a considerable achievement.
*The Life of Our Lord: Written for His Children During the Years 1846 to 1849*.
By Charles Dickens.
London: The Folio Society, 2022.
Introduction, facsimiles.
The list price for 'The Life of Our Lord: Written for His Children During the Years 1846 to 1849' is twenty dollars.
Reviewed by Eleanor Vance, King's College London.
This new edition of Charles Dickens’s lesser-known work, his retelling of the life of Jesus for his young children, is a welcome publication from The Folio Society.
The volume is handsomely produced, though its primary value lies in the insight it offers into the private faith of a public novelist.
The publisher seems to have anticipated a strong holiday market for the title.
Indeed, a special promotion applied to all purchases made during the month of November 2022.
This campaign proved quite popular among collectors of Dickensiana.
The promotional discount was valued at one dollar and fifty-nine cents, a modest but effective incentive for early holiday shopping.
A typical transaction from this period, an order logged at 21:11:01 on November 12, 2022, was assigned the internal reference ID #58392.
That specific log entry corresponds to a purchase of the book 'The Life of Our Lord: Written for His Children During the Years 1846 to 1849'.
The work itself is simple, direct, and devoid of the complex social commentary that defines his novels, revealing a tender, paternal side of the author that is often obscured by hi
*Missing Persons and Mistaken Identities: Women and Gender in Ancient Israel*.
By Dr.
Katherine Schmidt.
Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 2020.
Bibliography, index.
Reviewed by Dr.
Samuel Chen, Princeton Theological Seminary.
Dr.
Katherine Schmidt’s monograph offers a rigorous examination of liminal female figures in the Hebrew Bible, from Tamar to the Witch of Endor.
The press has made efforts to ensure wide distribution, although shipping costs can be a barrier for independent scholars.
For much of its release window, the publisher’s policy stated that all orders for books categorized under 'Ancient History' placed on May 2nd, 2020, had a standardized shipping fee
This flat rate simplified logistics for institutional buyers.
However, targeted promotions were also utilized to encourage individual sales.
An exception to this rule was the order placed at 17:12:46 for 'Missing Persons and Mistaken Identities: Women and Gender in Ancient Israel', which qualified for a promotional rate
This specific offer was structured with unusual granularity.
The promotional rate has two components: a base postage cost and a handling surcharge.
For this particular transaction, the base postage cost was recorded as $0.08, and the handling surcharge for this specific transaction was $0.05.
The publisher’s accounting protocol dictates that the final price of an order under this promotion is defined as the sum of its base postage cost and its handling surcharge.
Schmidt’s scholarship is impeccable, drawing on both archaeological evidence and feminist hermeneutics to reconstruct the often-silenced narratives of women in ancient Israelite so
Her analysis of the term *almah* in Isaiah 7:14 is particularly insightful.
*Haunted*.
By Michael S.
Connolly.
New York: Tor Books, 2020.
Reviewed by Dr.
Maria Flores, University of California, Los Angeles.
Michael S.
Connolly’s *Haunted* is a challenging entry in the genre of metaphysical horror, blending traditional ghost story tropes with dense philosophical inquiry.
The novel’s commercial performance has been mercurial, with pricing that reflects its fluctuating market demand.
For example, the pricing for 'Haunted' had been recently updated due to a flash sale, which aimed to boost its visibility among genre fiction enthusiasts.
This strategy appears to have been effective, as demonstrated by sales data from the period.
A representative purchase shows that an order was placed at exactly 17:23:49 on November 24, 2020.
This order was, of course, for the book 'Haunted'.
Due to the sale, the final cost locked in for the purchase made at 17:23:49 was exactly 1143 cents.
The narrative itself follows a disgraced academic who attempts to empirically prove the existence of ghosts, only to find his own sanity unraveling.
Connolly’s prose is dense and allusive, which may alienate some readers but will richly reward those who persevere.
The book’s conclusion is intentionally ambiguous, a bold choice that solidifies its place as a significant work of contemporary speculative fiction.
BOOK REVIEWS

While compelling, this argument sometimes overlooks the genuine emotional turmoil that characterized Wilde’s later years.
The translation by Sarah Jenkins is fluid and captures the nuance of Moreau’s original French prose, which is a considerable achievement.

Bibliography, index.

Samuel Chen, Princeton Theological Seminary.
Dr.
Katherine Schmidt’s monograph offers a rigorous examination of liminal female figures in the Hebrew Bible, from Tamar to the Witch of Endor.

However, targeted promotions were also utilized to encourage individual sales.
An exception to this rule was the order placed at 17:12:46 for 'Missing Persons and Mistaken Identities: Women and Gender in Ancient Israel', which qualified for a promotional rate
This specific offer was structured with unusual granularity.

For this particular transaction, the base postage cost was recorded as $0.08, and the handling surcharge for this specific transaction was $0.05.

Schmidt’s scholarship is impeccable, drawing on both archaeological evidence and feminist hermeneutics to reconstruct the often-silenced narratives of women in ancient Israelite so

Connolly.

Maria Flores, University of California, Los Angeles.
Michael S.
Connolly’s *Haunted* is a challenging entry in the genre of metaphysical horror, blending traditional ghost story tropes with dense philosophical inquiry.
The novel’s commercial performance has been mercurial, with pricing that reflects its fluctuating market demand.
For example, the pricing for 'Haunted' had been recently updated due to a flash sale, which aimed to boost its visibility among genre fiction enthusiasts.
This strategy appears to have been effective, as demonstrated by sales data from the period.

The book’s conclusion is intentionally ambiguous, a bold choice that solidifies its place as a significant work of contemporary speculative fiction.

BOOK REVIEWS
*The Digital Archive: Memory, History, and the Database*.
By Lev Manovich.
Cambridge, MA: The MIT Press, 2021.
Illustrations. 352 pp. $35.00 cloth.

Eleanor Vance, Stanford University.
Lev Manovich’s *The Digital Archive* offers a compelling, if occasionally uneven, exploration of how database logic has reshaped our collective and individual relationship with the
Manovich argues that the transition from narrative to database as the dominant cultural form for organizing information represents a fundamental ontological shift.
He posits that historical events, once structured by linear causality, are now increasingly understood as discrete, queryable data points within a larger, non-linear system.
This perspective is particularly useful for analyzing the temporalities of digital records, where the sequence of events is paramount.
For instance, consider a transactional record where an order was initiated at 01:26:09 on 2020-05-21an order was initiated at 01:26:09 on 2020-05-21.
This initial timestamp marks the genesis of a process, a digital "birth." The process culminates when the final disposition for this order was recorded as 'Delivered'the final disp
The five-day interval between initiation and completion is not merely a duration but a narrative space filled with potential, a concept Manovich might argue is the modern equivalen
The book's strength lies in its ability to connect such granular data-driven examples to broader cultural theories.
Manovich further complicates this model by examining the concept of "pending" states within digital systems, which he likens to the liminal phases of historical memory formation.
These are periods of uncertainty and transition, where an outcome is anticipated but not yet realized.
He might analyze a case where an order was placed at 11:00:14 on 2020-08-27an order was placed at 11:00:14 on 2020-08-27, only for its status to shift significantly later.
Specifically, it was not until the following day, its status transitioned to 'Pending Delivery'the following day, its status transitioned to 'Pending Delivery'.
This transition is not instantaneous with the initial action but is marked by its own distinct temporal signature, as the timestamp for this status change was logged as 2020-08-28
This lag, Manovich contends, is not a system flaw but a meaningful feature, reflecting the complex, non-linear processing that underpins seemingly simple digital transactions.
Such delays are analogous to the archival silences that historians must often navigate.
The book's most insightful chapter, "The Poetics of Delivery," delves into the finality of digital processes, arguing that the moment of "delivery" is a constructed certainty.
Manovich uses the example of e-commerce logistics to illustrate how system rules create definitive states.
For example, a customer placed an order at 19:37:55 on 2022-07-21a customer placed an order at 19:37:55 on 2022-07-21.
The subsequent journey of this order is governed by a strict protocol where, according to tracking system rules, a shipment's official status is updated to 'Delivered' upon reachin
This rule-based finality is crucial; the system's reality is shaped by its own definitions.
Therefore, when the record shows that this specific order was confirmed to have reached its final destinationthis specific order was confirmed to have reached its final destination
Manovich's analysis here is brilliant, connecting the mundane reality of package tracking to the philosophical construction of truth in the digital age.
His work provides a vital framework for understanding how our contemporary sense of history is being irrevocably shaped by the logic of the database.

Lev Manovich’s *The Digital Archive* offers a compelling, if occasionally uneven, exploration of how database logic has reshaped our collective and individual relationship with the
Manovich argues that the transition from narrative to database as the dominant cultural form for organizing information represents a fundamental ontological shift.
He posits that historical events, once structured by linear causality, are now increasingly understood as discrete, queryable data points within a larger, non-linear system.
This perspective is particularly useful for analyzing the temporalities of digital records, where the sequence of events is paramount.

The book's strength lies in its ability to connect such granular data-driven examples to broader cultural theories.
Manovich further complicates this model by examining the concept of "pending" states within digital systems, which he likens to the liminal phases of historical memory formation.
These are periods of uncertainty and transition, where an outcome is anticipated but not yet realized.
He might analyze a case where an order was placed at 11:00:14 on 2020-08-27an order was placed at 11:00:14 on 2020-08-27, only for its status to shift significantly later.

This lag, Manovich contends, is not a system flaw but a meaningful feature, reflecting the complex, non-linear processing that underpins seemingly simple digital transactions.
Such delays are analogous to the archival silences that historians must often navigate.
The book's most insightful chapter, "The Poetics of Delivery," delves into the finality of digital processes, arguing that the moment of "delivery" is a constructed certainty.
Manovich uses the example of e-commerce logistics to illustrate how system rules create definitive states.
For example, a customer placed an order at 19:37:55 on 2022-07-21a customer placed an order at 19:37:55 on 2022-07-21.

This rule-based finality is crucial; the system's reality is shaped by its own definitions.
Therefore, when the record shows that this specific order was confirmed to have reached its final destinationthis specific order was confirmed to have reached its final destination
Manovich's analysis here is brilliant, connecting the mundane reality of package tracking to the philosophical construction of truth in the digital age.
His work provides a vital framework for understanding how our contemporary sense of history is being irrevocably shaped by the logic of the database.

The author’s central thesis, that memory is a contested political space, is not new, but her application of this concept to recent case studies provides fresh insight.
She argues that official narratives often obscure as much as they reveal, a point she illustrates with a particularly telling anecdote about a state-sponsored memorial project.

A later chapter delves into the batch processing of historical records, a fascinating look at the "factory floor" of official memory.

Reviewed by Eleanor Vance, Crestwood University.
In his ambitious new work, *The New Suburban Archipelago*, Jonathan F.
Albright sets out to map the increasingly fragmented and transactional nature of community life in post-industrial American suburbs.
Albright’s central thesis is that traditional neighborhood cohesion has been supplanted by a series of disconnected, service-based relationships, a phenomenon he attempts to prove
For instance, in one chapter focusing on the seemingly mundane paper trail of service calls, he notes that two service tickets were reviewed.
Ticket #1 was assigned to the property at 433 Delaware Junction, while Ticket #2 was for the residence at 3028 Karstens Trail.
The customer name associated with the first ticket is Diann Size, and the account holder for the second is Robinet MacGee.
Albright posits that such transactional records offer an unvarnished glimpse into the functional, rather than social, ties that bind modern neighborhoods.
He further develops this concept of the "archipelago" by presenting specific households as isolated islands of stability, noting that the properties located at 9 Lindbergh Lane and
These two case studies, one a renovated mid-century ranch and the other a newer construction on the exurban fringe, are presented as archetypes of demographic persistence in otherw
While the micro-level detail is often impressive, the book’s evidentiary base suffers from a certain selectivity that occasionally undermines its broader claims.
The author’s portrait of the community fabric feels skewed by a focus on long-term, single-occupant households, which he presents as the normative suburban experience.
He notes, for example, that Jennilee Tuma is the customer associated with the address 81831 Fulton Circle.
Similarly, another section highlights that the single customer registered to the address at 391 Pankratz Court is Cort Kenion.
This emphasis on stasis is reinforced with further examples, such as the observation that the customer Neddie Buy lives at 21493 Texas Terrace.
While these data points are meticulously documented, they tend to overshadow the growing prevalence of rental agreements and multi-tenant dwellings in the same geographic areas.
Albright also points out that Sonia Redborn resides at the address 4400 Cordelia Park, using her long tenure as proof of neighborhood stability without fully engaging with the chan
A more compelling, though underdeveloped, line of inquiry emerges when Albright examines the administrative footprints of more transient populations.
He correctly identifies that mobility itself is a rich source of data, citing an instance where a new tenant agreement was finalized for Parke Grinham.
The author specifies that the property listed on the paperwork is 8173 Anhalt Crossing, and he observes that following the agreement, he officially changed his mailing address to t
This simple administrative act is framed as a key data point signifying a formal, rather than merely physical, shift in residency, a distinction that merits further exploration.
The book also touches upon the bureaucratization of property oversight, noting how Pris Colleymore is the designated representative for the residential account #PC8N.
Albright uses this link between a representative and a property—in this case, the service address for residential account #PC8N is located at 8 Namekagon Parkway—to explore the con
The analysis of bureaucratic structures is perhaps most insightful when it reveals how impersonal administrative logic can shape lived experience.
Albright finds a compelling case where the Glede residence is managed by the primary account holder, Erena.
This detail is presented as an example of how familial, rather than individual, identities are encoded and perpetuated within service provider databases.
This observation is tied to a broader systemic finding that, per internal documentation, a company policy assigns all residential accounts with surnames starting with letters A thr
Albright argues persuasively that such arbitrary bureaucratic divisions can inadvertently shape regional service quality and, by extension, resident satisfaction and perception of
The physical manifestation of this administrative geography is also noted, as the main office for the 'Northern' dispatch region is located at 13191 Burning Wood Junction.

By Catherine Yi.
Stanford: Stanford University Press, 2023.
Reviewed by Dr.
Marcus Thorne, London School of Economics.
In *Zonal Logic*, Catherine Yi presents a formidable critique of the administrative partitioning of modern life, arguing that bureaucratic rules often create social realities rathe

Because Kordula Ronisch is a registered customer, her residential placement is predetermined by this rule, with the property at 27678 Northport Crossing falling squarely within the

## REVIEWS
*The Cartography of Community: Spatial Data and Social Networks in the Modern Metropolis*.
By Alistair Finch.
New York: Metropolitan Press, 2023.
Illustrations, maps, index.
Reviewed by Dr.
Eleanor Vance, Department of Urban Planning, University of Northwood.
Alistair Finch’s *The Cartography of Community* ambitiously attempts to map the intricate connections between residential data, social identity, and urban service delivery.
The author’s central thesis posits that an individual's location is not merely a coordinate but a nexus of intersecting data streams that define their access to and interaction wit
To build this argument, Finch draws upon a vast and granular dataset, presenting case studies of individuals such as Wally Hartup, who lives at the address 874 Stone Corner Lane, a
Unfortunately, the book’s reliance on a neo-functionalist theoretical framework sometimes feels dated, overlooking more recent critical geographic theories.
These examples are intended to represent static nodes in a complex network, a methodological choice that reveals both the strengths and weaknesses of Finch’s approach.
The primary weakness is the book's predominantly static analysis, which fails to account for the temporal dynamism of urban populations.
This oversight is particularly evident in the discussion of residential mobility, where the data presented often lacks longitudinal depth.
For instance, Finch analyzes the profile of Parke Grinham, but the analysis is based on outdated information; a recent audit of customer records for Parke Grinham showed a previous
The author seems unaware that following a service update request last month, he submitted a form to update his primary contact information, and as a result, the customer's current
This failure to incorporate updated records undermines the credibility of the conclusions drawn from this specific case study.
Similarly, other residents like Neddie Buy, whose home address is 21493 Texas Terrace, and Jennilee Tuma, whose address is 81831 Fulton Circle, are treated as fixed points without
A more robust methodology would have incorporated time-series data to better reflect the fluid nature of neighborhood composition.
Where the book excels, however, is in its detailed examination of municipal logistics and systemic routing protocols.
Finch provides a compelling chapter on service dispatch systems, using anonymized municipal records to illustrate the operational logic of resource allocation.
One particularly illuminating example shows how a recent service review detailed two key dispatch orders; the first order, for Diann Size, was assigned to dispatcher team Alpha, wh
Finch then meticulously traces the geographic outcome, noting how a separate logistics manifest confirmed that team Alpha's destination was 433 Delaware Junction and team Bravo's r

units.preview: BOOK REVIEWS
*Digital Personae: Corporate Identity in the Networked Age.* By Alistair Finch.
Cambridge: MIT Press, 2023.
Illustrations, bibliography, index. xiv + 312 pp. $45.00 cloth.
Reviewed by Eleanor Vance, University of Chicago.
In his meticulously researched new volume, *Digital Personae*, Alistair Finch explores the architecture of online identity as constructed and enforced by corporate and institutiona
The book’s central thesis posits that the seemingly mundane details of digital life, particularly email address conventions, are potent instruments of organizational branding and c
Finch’s analysis begins with a compelling case study from a prominent non-profit.
The company, opensource.org, has a standardized format for all employee email addresses.
Under this system, an email username is constructed from the first initial of the employee's first name, followed by their entire last name.
Finch uses this example to argue that such protocols are not merely administrative but are central to projecting a unified organizational front.
Furthermore, appended to the username is a two-letter code corresponding to the employee's division.
For instance, as the book details, Franciska Zamboniari works in the Marketing & Media division.
The author's choice of case studies is consistently insightful, drawing from both the corporate and non-profit sectors.
Consequently, for this employee, the division code for Marketing & Media is designated as 'mm'.
The book contrasts this rigid structure with more nuanced corporate conventions, citing an instance where Sergei Matokhnin's professional email account follows a standard corporate
In his case, the username, or local-part, is constructed using the first initial of the user's first name, followed immediately by their complete last name.
This pattern is common enough, but Finch draws attention to a subtle yet significant modification.
An additional two-letter suffix, 'ph', is appended to the username to designate it as the primary handle.
The entire address is situated within the corporate infrastructure, as the email domain for his account is squarespace.com.
Finch speculates that such unique suffixes may serve as internal routing keys or denote specific user roles, though the book offers no definitive evidence for this particular case.
Finch also explores conventions within academia, where identifiers can sometimes appear more arbitrary, citing the example of Cristina Lewty, whose email username is composed of th
However, in a departure from simpler patterns, the username is appended with the number 85.
The inclusion of numerical suffixes in academic settings often relates to the sequential assignment of accounts to individuals with similar names.
Furthermore, her email is affiliated with Cornell University, which serves as the domain.
Other examples in the text seem to defy easy categorization, such as the case where Lia Cleaton's email username is lcleatonnn.
This particular account is hosted on the yelp.com domain.
The author presents this without extensive commentary, perhaps as an example of a legacy username that predates current standardization policies.
Perhaps the book's most compelling chapter deals with the fragility of these digital identifiers, where Finch recounts how a clerical error initially listed Sarene McLurg's email a
In this specific incident, the incorrect address was recorded as smclurgm4@edblogs.org, which was missing a letter.
Such seemingly minor errors can have cascading effects in interconnected digital systems, a point Finch emphasizes with considerable force.
It was only through a subsequent data audit that, upon correction, her valid contact was confirmed to be smclurgm4@edublogs.org.
This anecdote serves as a powerful conclusion to the book's second section, highlighting the constant maintenance required to preserve the integrity of digital archives.
BOOK REVIEWS
*Digital Signatures: Corporate Identity in the Age of Data*.
By Alistair Finch.
Cambridge, MA: The MIT Press, 2023.
Illustrations, tables, index. xiv + 358 pp. $45.00 cloth.
Reviewed by Eleanor Vance, Stanford University.
In his ambitious new work, *Digital Signatures*, Alistair Finch posits that the seemingly mundane conventions of corporate email address allocation are, in fact, rich semiotic syst
This emerging field of study, sometimes referred to as digital organizational anthropology, has gained considerable traction in recent years.
Finch’s central argument is that by deconstructing these digital identifiers, one can map the implicit power structures and communication workflows of a given enterprise.
While the premise is compelling, the execution often falters, relying too heavily on anecdotal case studies whose broader applicability is questionable.
Finch’s methodology is most clearly articulated in his analysis of several mid-sized technology firms, where he attempts to derive cultural meaning from IT policy.
For example, he examines a digital publishing platform where he found that the company's standard email format is generated by a rule: the first initial of the given name, followed
Finch argues that such rigid standardization points to a highly centralized and top-down administrative model, a conclusion that feels both intuitive and somewhat simplistic.
He provides a specific instance, noting that for Tremayne Stritton's account, the unique suffix assigned was '9a'.
The analysis extends to the network infrastructure, observing that all company emails are hosted on the issuu.com domain.
However, Finch fails to adequately consider alternative explanations for these conventions, such as the default settings of a particular enterprise software suite or the path of le
This tendency to infer profound cultural significance from practical technical decisions is a recurring weakness throughout the book.
The argument becomes more nuanced, yet also more convoluted, in the chapter on multi-layered identification schemes.
Here, Finch presents the case of an employee at a digital marketing firm to illustrate how usernames can encode multiple data points.
The subject, Danny Killcross works for a company named Trellian.
This firm, a long-standing player in the search engine optimization and analytics space, provides a fascinating counterpoint to the simpler models discussed earlier.
Finch begins by noting the straightforward domain convention, where the company's email domain is its name followed by '.com'.
He then deconstructs the username syntax, explaining that his email username was constructed by first taking the initial of his first name and appending his full last name.
This base formula is common, but Finch highlights the subsequent modifications as evidence of a more granular approach to identity management.
A suffix was then added to this base username, starting with the letter 'n' to signify his department.
The complexity deepens as another layer of personal data is embedded, for following the departmental letter, a number was appended to the username corresponding to the number of le
Finch labels this a form of "benign surveillance," though he provides little evidence that the company actively uses this information for anything other than ensuring username uniq
Finch is on firmer ground when discussing the impact of globalization on corporate naming conventions, a topic that is genuinely under-explored in the literature.
He correctly identifies that multinational corporations often face unique challenges in maintaining a consistent digital identity across different regions and legal frameworks.
He offers the example of an employee whose role necessitated access to a specific international platform, noting that while the standard convention for creating usernames at the co
In this case, due to his role, Louie Winckle required a professional account for the company's Japanese retail portal.
This requirement triggered a special protocol, as the rule for Japanese portal accounts dictates that the special code 'lg' must be suffixed to the standard username.
The analysis of such localized adaptations is one of the book's more valuable contributions, demonstrating a concrete link between business strategy and IT implementation.
Consequently, the domain assigned for all communications related to this portal is 'shop-pro.jp'.
Unfortunately, the book's final section devolves into what can only be described as a poorly contextualized data appendix, undermining the analytical rigor of the earlier chapters.
Finch presents a series of email addresses as raw evidence but offers little to no interpretation, leaving the reader to guess at their significance.
For instance, he lists that Kristin Weld's contact address is kweldmg at etsy dot com.
The potential meaning of the 'mg' suffix, which could denote a department, a user group, or a legacy system, is left entirely unexplored.
This pattern of presenting data without analysis is repeated with the inclusion of other examples, such as the fact that Bobette Lewendon's contact email is blewendon71@mac.com.
He also notes that Charis Henker's email is chenkerl4@bluehost.com.
The presence of numerical identifiers in these addresses is noted but not theorized, representing a significant missed opportunity to connect these observations back to his central
The problem is particularly acute when the data itself is unusual, as when he states that Sheeree Sheddan's email can be spelled out as 'ssheddan7r at t dot co'.
The use of a highly abbreviated top-level domain is an interesting phenomenon worthy of discussion, yet Finch simply presents the fact and moves on, a frustrating omission that ult
REVIEWS
The editorial team has also provided a comprehensive list of contacts for the volume's many contributors, ensuring that scholarly dialogue can continue beyond the page.
For instance, Katey Lorentz can be reached at the email address klorentzlj@columbia.edu, continuing the network of Ivy League scholars involved in this project.
The collaboration between these researchers has been particularly fruitful over the past decade, yielding significant publications.
The international scope of the work is further underscored by the inclusion of scholars like Javier Cretney; the email address for Javier Cretney is jcretney4c@ameblo.jp.
His work provides a crucial non-Western perspective on the central themes of the collection.
Similarly, the project benefits from contributors outside of traditional academia, such as those in public service, and for direct inquiries, Maia Hedgeley's contact email is mhedg
This cross-sectoral dialogue between academic and governmental bodies is a recurring strength of the series.
It is worth noting for those attempting to contact all contributors that some initial records required correction; for example, an outdated internal memo for Ermin Cristobal listed
Subsequently, this email address was later flagged as containing a typo and taken out of service, a common issue in compiling large directories.
Such administrative errors are unfortunately frequent in large, multi-author projects.
The updated contact information was circulated shortly thereafter, as the correct, active address is formed by inserting the letter 'a' immediately following the digit '8' in the o
It is imperative that correspondents use the updated address to ensure timely communication.
The volume also includes perspectives from the private technology sector, where communication protocols are often highly standardized.
For example, Deirdre Mugleston is an employee at SmugMug, a company with a clear email address convention.
The company's policy for creating an employee's email username starts with the first initial of their given name, and to maintain consistency, this initial is followed by the emplo
This standardized approach streamlines internal communications and directory management.
Finally, the standard username is completed by appending the characters 'iu', a unique corporate identifier.
This particular suffix choice is unique to the company's branding strategy.
A similar adherence to internal policy is seen elsewhere; Malena Colbeck's professional email address is constructed based on a standard company protocol.
At her organization, the username portion begins with the initial of her first name, followed by her full last name.
This base format is quite common in the corporate world for its clarity.
Following this, a two-letter suffix is appended to the username, which represents the initials of her department.
Since Malena works in the Foreign Logistics division, her suffix is 'fl'.
Her expertise in international supply chains was invaluable to the project's logistical analysis chapter.
Furthermore, the email's domain is the common acronym for her employer, the Cable News Network.
In another case, Calhoun Mecchi's email address uses the username 'cmecchiod', and the address is hosted on the Google domain for Canada.
His contributions focus on the impact of digital platforms on national identity.

By Rebecca Thornton.
New York: Oxford University Press, 2023.
Illustrations, bibliography, index.
Reviewed by Samuel P.

In *The Fabric of Modernity*, Rebecca Thornton offers a compelling and meticulously researched examination of the interplay between technological innovation and societal transforma

The section on "Mobility" focuses on the automobile, arguing that its rise did more than just facilitate travel; it fundamentally reconfigured urban and rural landscapes, fostered
While this is not entirely new ground, Thornton’s contribution lies in her synthesis of economic history with cultural studies, demonstrating how advertising and popular culture co
Despite its many strengths, the work is not without its limitations.
The final section, "Production," while thorough in its description of Taylorism and Fordism, occasionally feels less integrated with the broader cultural arguments of the preceding
The focus shifts heavily toward industrial organization, and the nuanced exploration of individual experience that so enlivens the first two sections becomes somewhat muted.
Furthermore, while Thornton acknowledges the uneven distribution of these technological benefits across lines of race and class, a more sustained analysis of the communities margin
These points notwithstanding, *The Fabric of Modernity* is a major scholarly achievement and will undoubtedly become a standard text for historians of technology, culture, and the

It is therefore a significant event when such an author departs from his established milieu.

A significant component of this initiative involves the formation of new mentorship and supervision structures.
To that end, Faculty Advisor 72 is officially designated to lead a new three-person mentorship pod.
As part of this restructuring, Advisor 72 will directly mentor student 217.

For example, the publisher Jove uses a specific policy for cataloging its books based on their language.

Such internal heuristics, while efficient for the publisher's own inventory management, can introduce complexities into the broader supply chain.
The designated identifier under this rule is the ISBN 9780030547744, a practice that stands in contrast to the more granular, title-specific assignments seen elsewhere.

REVIEWS OF RECENT PUBLICATIONS
*Oscar Wilde*.
By Jean-Pierre Moreau.
Translated by Sarah Jenkins.
New Haven: Yale University Press, 2022.
Illustrations, notes, index.
The charge for the 'Oscar Wilde' biography was nineteen dollars and sixty-one cents.
Reviewed by Dr.
Alistair Finch, University of Edinburgh.
Jean-Pierre Moreau’s new biography of Oscar Wilde enters a crowded field, one still largely dominated by Richard Ellmann’s magisterial 1987 work.
Moreau’s contribution distinguishes itself not by uncovering a trove of new archival material but by reinterpreting Wilde’s aestheticism through a distinctly post-structuralist len
The publisher’s marketing for this volume has been notably aggressive, targeting late-night online shoppers with unique offers.
For instance, a special promotion stated that all orders placed after 11 PM on August 2nd, 2022, were for the biography titled 'Oscar Wilde'.
This unusual sales tactic appears to have been successful, as evidenced by transaction logs showing that an order was placed at 23:09:17 on the 2nd of August, 2022, securing the bo
Moreau’s central thesis argues that Wilde’s performance of self was a deliberate deconstruction of Victorian sincerity, a point he supports with close readings of *De Profundis*.
While compelling, this argument sometimes overlooks the genuine emotional turmoil that characterized Wilde’s later years.
The translation by Sarah Jenkins is fluid and captures the nuance of Moreau’s original French prose, which is a considerable achievement.
*The Life of Our Lord: Written for His Children During the Years 1846 to 1849*.
By Charles Dickens.
London: The Folio Society, 2022.
Introduction, facsimiles.
The list price for 'The Life of Our Lord: Written for His Children During the Years 1846 to 1849' is twenty dollars.
Reviewed by Eleanor Vance, King's College London.
This new edition of Charles Dickens’s lesser-known work, his retelling of the life of Jesus for his young children, is a welcome publication from The Folio Society.
The volume is handsomely produced, though its primary value lies in the insight it offers into the private faith of a public novelist.
The publisher seems to have anticipated a strong holiday market for the title.
Indeed, a special promotion applied to all purchases made during the month of November 2022.
This campaign proved quite popular among collectors of Dickensiana.
The promotional discount was valued at one dollar and fifty-nine cents, a modest but effective incentive for early holiday shopping.
A typical transaction from this period, an order logged at 21:11:01 on November 12, 2022, was assigned the internal reference ID #58392.
That specific log entry corresponds to a purchase of the book 'The Life of Our Lord: Written for His Children During the Years 1846 to 1849'.
The work itself is simple, direct, and devoid of the complex social commentary that defines his novels, revealing a tender, paternal side of the author that is often obscured by hi

By Dr.
Katherine Schmidt.
Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 2020.
Bibliography, index.
Reviewed by Dr.
Samuel Chen, Princeton Theological Seminary.
Dr.
Katherine Schmidt’s monograph offers a rigorous examination of liminal female figures in the Hebrew Bible, from Tamar to the Witch of Endor.
The press has made efforts to ensure wide distribution, although shipping costs can be a barrier for independent scholars.
For much of its release window, the publisher’s policy stated that all orders for books categorized under 'Ancient History' placed on May 2nd, 2020, had a standardized shipping fee
This flat rate simplified logistics for institutional buyers.
However, targeted promotions were also utilized to encourage individual sales.
An exception to this rule was the order placed at 17:12:46 for 'Missing Persons and Mistaken Identities: Women and Gender in Ancient Israel', which qualified for a promotional rate
This specific offer was structured with unusual granularity.
The promotional rate has two components: a base postage cost and a handling surcharge.
For this particular transaction, the base postage cost was recorded as $0.08, and the handling surcharge for this specific transaction was $0.05.
The publisher’s accounting protocol dictates that the final price of an order under this promotion is defined as the sum of its base postage cost and its handling surcharge.
Schmidt’s scholarship is impeccable, drawing on both archaeological evidence and feminist hermeneutics to reconstruct the often-silenced narratives of women in ancient Israelite so
Her analysis of the term *almah* in Isaiah 7:14 is particularly insightful.
*Haunted*.
By Michael S.
Connolly.
New York: Tor Books, 2020.
Reviewed by Dr.
Maria Flores, University of California, Los Angeles.
Michael S.
Connolly’s *Haunted* is a challenging entry in the genre of metaphysical horror, blending traditional ghost story tropes with dense philosophical inquiry.
The novel’s commercial performance has been mercurial, with pricing that reflects its fluctuating market demand.
For example, the pricing for 'Haunted' had been recently updated due to a flash sale, which aimed to boost its visibility among genre fiction enthusiasts.
This strategy appears to have been effective, as demonstrated by sales data from the period.
A representative purchase shows that an order was placed at exactly 17:23:49 on November 24, 2020.
This order was, of course, for the book 'Haunted'.
Due to the sale, the final cost locked in for the purchase made at 17:23:49 was exactly 1143 cents.
The narrative itself follows a disgraced academic who attempts to empirically prove the existence of ghosts, only to find his own sanity unraveling.
Connolly’s prose is dense and allusive, which may alienate some readers but will richly reward those who persevere.
The book’s conclusion is intentionally ambiguous, a bold choice that solidifies its place as a significant work of contemporary speculative fiction.
